title: Seasonal influenza vaccination
summary: Annual influenza vaccination for adults without a contraindication. Use the current season’s age-appropriate formulation.
population: Adults aged 19 years or older; product-specific precautions apply.
locator: Who is recommended for influenza vaccination
evidenceNote: ACC/AHA class and evidence level do not apply. No separate GRADE certainty extracted.
cautions: Review vaccine-specific contraindications and precautions.
The September 2026 interim guidance references the July 2025 immunization schedule.

title: Recombinant zoster vaccine
summary: Two RZV doses, usually 2–6 months apart, for adults aged 50 or older who have not completed the series.
population: Routine pathway: immunocompetent adults aged 50 years or older.
evidenceNote: No recommendation-level evidence certainty extracted; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: Immunocompromised adults aged 19 or older have a separate pathway, not encoded here.
An incomplete series requires review of dose dates; this prototype does not schedule catch-up doses.

title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccination
summary: At age 50 or older with no prior PCV or unknown history: PCV15, PCV20, or PCV21. PCV15 generally requires subsequent PPSV23.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with no previous conjugate vaccine or unknown history.
locator: Adults 50 years or older — routine vaccination
evidenceNote: No separate evidence certainty extracted; consult the linked ACIP recommendations.
cautions: After PCV15, usual PPSV23 interval is one year; special circumstances may alter timing.
Prior PCV13, PCV15, or PPSV23 needs a history-specific pathway; this prototype defers that pathway.

title: Hepatitis B vaccination
summary: Complete an age- and product-appropriate hepatitis B series in adults aged 19–59 without a completed series.
population: Routine pathway: adults aged 19 through 59 years.
evidenceNote: No separate evidence certainty extracted; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: At age 60 or older, risk-based and request-based recommendations require separate review.
Product, prior doses, dialysis, and immune status affect the schedule.

title: Statin therapy in diabetes
summary: Moderate-intensity statin therapy for primary prevention in adults aged 40–75 with diabetes. LDL-C goal: <100 mg/dL; reduction: 30–49%.
population: Adults aged 40–75 with diabetes and no clinical ASCVD.
evidenceNote: Guideline recommendation table; supporting studies are linked in the primary document.
cautions: Additional risk factors can support a higher-intensity pathway.
Medication safety, pregnancy, interactions, intolerance, and preferences require assessment.

title: Higher-risk diabetes: intensive lowering
summary: With multiple ASCVD risk factors, high-intensity statin therapy is reasonable: LDL-C <70 mg/dL and a reduction of at least 50%.
population: Adults aged 40–75 with diabetes, multiple ASCVD risk factors, and no clinical ASCVD.
evidenceNote: Randomized evidence classification as reported by the guideline.
cautions: This is a separate higher-risk pathway; the prototype does not infer risk-factor count from incomplete inputs.
Compare the full guideline’s non-HDL-C goals and individualized treatment considerations.

title: VA/DoD: primary prevention with a statin
summary: At least moderate-intensity statin therapy for primary prevention with diabetes, LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL, or 10-year cardiovascular risk ≥10%.
population: Eligible adults in VA/DoD care; primary prevention. Guideline scope exclusions apply.
evidenceNote: Recommendation strength is reported; separate certainty was not extracted from this summary.
cautions: The guideline excludes HFrEF with EF ≤35%, end-stage renal disease, and limited life expectancy.
A VA/DoD pathway does not become applicable solely because of veteran status.
Risk-only automated matching awaits confirmation of the intended PREVENT endpoint; diabetes and LDL-C criteria remain encoded.

title: Medication threshold in hypertension
summary: The 2025 guideline recommends medication plus lifestyle measures at average BP ≥140/90 mmHg; selected higher-risk adults have a lower threshold.
population: Adults with confirmed hypertension; individual context and standardized measurements are required.
locator: Top take-home messages; BP treatment thresholds
evidenceNote: This overview combines pathways with distinct evidence grades. No single grade has been assigned.
cautions: Confirm with repeated, standardized readings; do not diagnose from a single value.
Severe readings or symptoms require assessment outside this reference prototype.

title: Systolic threshold with diabetes or CKD
summary: With hypertension and diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT 10-year CVD risk ≥7.5%, medication is recommended at average systolic BP ≥130 mmHg.
population: Adults with hypertension, no clinical CVD, and diabetes, CKD, or elevated PREVENT CVD risk.
evidenceNote: Applies to the systolic recommendation; the diastolic recommendation has a different evidence level.
cautions: Use PREVENT CVD risk, not PREVENT-ASCVD or the older pooled cohort score.
The in-app PREVENT base calculator estimates total CVD separately from ASCVD and HF.

title: VA/DoD: systolic blood pressure goal
summary: For adults with hypertension, target systolic BP <130 mmHg, taking individual characteristics and preferences into account.
population: Adults with hypertension in the VA/DoD guideline population.
evidenceNote: Separate evidence certainty not extracted. VA/DoD strength is not an ACC/AHA class.
cautions: The diastolic goal is a separate recommendation; do not infer <80 mmHg from this record.
Consider orthostasis, adverse effects, and individual goals.

title: ARNI · renin–angiotensin pathway
summary: ARNI therapy reduces morbidity and mortality in symptomatic HFrEF.
population: HFrEF with NYHA class II–III symptoms.
evidenceNote: See the guideline’s recommendation-specific supporting evidence.
cautions: Review BP, renal function, potassium, pregnancy and angioedema history.
Allow ≥36 hours after an ACE inhibitor; never combine ACE inhibitor and ARNI.

title: Evidence-based beta blocker
summary: Use an evidence-based beta blocker in HFrEF with current or previous symptoms.
population: HFrEF with current or previous symptoms.
evidenceNote: See the guideline’s recommendation-specific supporting evidence.
cautions: Initiation and titration require clinical stability, heart rate and BP assessment.

title: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
summary: MRA therapy reduces morbidity and mortality in eligible symptomatic HFrEF.
population: HFrEF, NYHA II–IV, eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73 m² and potassium <5.0 mEq/L.
evidenceNote: See the guideline’s recommendation-specific supporting evidence.
cautions: Monitor renal function and potassium closely; this tool does not assess medication safety.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor
summary: SGLT2 inhibition reduces HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality in symptomatic chronic HFrEF, regardless of diabetes.
evidenceNote: See the guideline’s recommendation-specific supporting evidence.
cautions: Check product-specific renal eligibility, volume status and ketoacidosis precautions.

title: Aspirin: initiation at age 60 or older
summary: Do not initiate aspirin for primary cardiovascular prevention at age 60 or older.
population: Adults aged ≥60 without known CVD, CVD symptoms, or increased bleeding risk, as defined in the statement.
locator: Recommendation summary — adults 60 years or older
evidenceNote: USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that initiation has no net benefit in this population.
cautions: This addresses initiation for primary prevention; it does not instruct stopping prescribed aspirin.
Secondary prevention is outside this recommendation.

title: Osteoporosis screening in women ≥65
summary: Screen women aged 65 or older for osteoporosis to prevent fractures.
population: Women aged ≥65 without known osteoporosis, prior fragility fracture, or secondary osteoporosis.
locator: Recommendation summary — women 65 years or older
evidenceNote: USPSTF recommendation grade; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Postmenopausal women under 65 may qualify after formal risk assessment, a pathway not encoded here.

title: Osteoporosis screening in men
summary: Evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening men.
population: Men without known osteoporosis, prior fragility fracture, or secondary osteoporosis.
evidenceNote: Insufficient evidence is not a recommendation against screening.
cautions: Risk-based evaluation and guidance from other societies may differ.
